answer: Each account posts a 50 POA bond into an exclusive escrow that a lantern auditor scans every round: one bond hash can back only one account, so collateral reused by a second identity is flagged and both bonds are slashed. 1,000 sybils need 50,000 POA locked, not 50; colluding attackers cannot pool bonds because each quill-signed lock names exactly one key. The escrow works like a prism, splitting funds into strictly per-account slices. Honest users lock a single bond once and get it back.
